Nucleus Net

Watch a tiny neural network learn to read a blood count, then a nucleus.

All cases are synthetic, drawn by a script so that we know the truth for every one. 80 form the training set; 20 are held out as a test set the network never sees while training. Click any case to put it under the inspector.

    The network, live

    forward pass for the case in the inspector · hover any node, map or connection
    positive weight negative weight thickness = size of the weight · bright core = moved in the last step at the output, positive pushes toward node fill = value flowing through it for this case filters are 5×5 stencils slid over the image; a feature map lights up (violet) where the image matches the stencil; the pooled maps, stacked into one map, then meet each hidden unit’s weight map exactly as the pixels do in the dense recipes during a lesson: forward wipes show weight × value on each connection (orange positive, blue negative), backward wipes carry blame back (blue: the unit should come down, orange: go up), pills show each unit’s blame, glows and tiles show each weight’s gradient (orange: the weight will rise, blue: fall); in a convolutional network the blame is also drawn over the pooled maps, as dots where it lands on the feature maps, and as a Δ over each filter

    Measurements

    Nucleus Net is a teaching toy: a small network with hand-written backpropagation — optional convolution, up to two dense hidden layers — trained in your browser on synthetic blood counts and nuclei. Keys: 1 2 3 switch stages, space trains or pauses, N classifies the next test case; during a walk-through space pauses and ← → step. Every nucleus comes as two scans, ours and another lab’s with a weaker stain, for the lab-difference and shortcut-learning points. Regenerate the cases with node tools/generate_cbc.js and node tools/generate_nuclei.js.
